lines.x: Argentina's country risk index calculated by JP Morgan fell below 900 points as dollar-denominated bonds rebounded following earlier losses.
Argentine sovereign risk surpassed 850 points as local stocks fell up to 8% in Wall Street trading, wholesale the US dollar weakened, and the central bank purchased USD 9 million.
Argentina's sovereign peso bonds fell following a surge in trading and prices that sparked speculation of government intervention to lower borrowing costs ahead of Treasury auctions.
Argentine shares dropped in New York trading on November 4, led by a 7.1% decline in YPF and a 5.4% drop in Pampa Energía amid a broader oil slump, while the peso held near 1,548 per dollar.
